#Overview

This document presents the analyses for the two Study 2 post-tests. 

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(comment=NA, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, echo=FALSE)
library(psych)
library(knitr)
library(tidyr)
library(broom)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggthemes)
library(gridExtra)
library(dplyr)
```

#Part 1: Self Evaluation Data Cleaning and Merging

##T1 Data

We read in the data file that we finished our Study 2 analysis with, including all of our indices, and only the participants who passed the attention check, followed instructions, and didn't take the survey more than once. In this data file, I begin the analysis with the unanonymized data (non-public), for MID matching purposes. The merged anonymized file is available on OSF.

```{r}
d_T1 <- read.csv("Study 2 with indices nonanon.csv") #Includes only people who weren't excluded in Study 1
d_T1$condition <- as.factor(d_T1$condition)
```

#T2 - Self evaluation

In total, 948 people returned for the T2 survey. In our analysis, we only include those who passed the T1 attention check, followed instructions, etc., leaving 855 participants at T2.

```{r}
d_T2self <- read.csv("T2 self - full data.csv")
d <- merge(d_T1, d_T2self, all=FALSE)

returningMIDs <- d$MID
didntreturn <- d_T1 %>%
  filter(!(MID %in% returningMIDs))

table(d$condition)
table(didntreturn$condition)

exclusion_table <- rbind(table(d$condition), table(didntreturn$condition))

chisq.test(exclusion_table)
```

Theres no difference by condition in rate of return (p = .65).

\newpage

# Argument Strength

At T2, participants see their original argument and judge the argument strength, without being reminded of their condition. The argument strength index participants answered at T2 consists of 6 questions:

- How persuasive is this argument?

- How convincing is this argument?

- How reasonable is this argument?

- How strong is this argument?

- How thoughtful is this argument?

- How well-formulated is this argument?

#Creating an index for argument strength

We begin by computing the alpha for argument strength:

```{r}
strengthItems <- dplyr::select(d, Q1.persuasive, Q2.convincing, Q3.reasonable, Q4.strong, Q5.thoughtful, Q6.wellformulated)
alphaStrength <- psych::alpha(strengthItems)
kable(alphaStrength$total)
```

Because our alpha is acceptable (alpha = 0.94), we then combine the 6 argument strength items into a single index.
```{r}
d$strengthIndex <- (d$Q1.persuasive + d$Q2.convincing + d$Q3.reasonable + d$Q4.strong + d$Q5.thoughtful + d$Q6.wellformulated)/6
```


\newpage

# Effect of original condition on argument strength

We use the same contrasts as in the main analysis of Study 2, first comparing PT - different to same and control, then comparing same and control to one another. 

#Run the regression
```{r}
d$condition <- as.factor(d$condition)
contrasts(d$condition) <- cbind(c(-1, 2, -1), c(+1, 0, -1))
strengthmodel <- lm(strengthIndex ~ condition, d)
```

##Omnibus Anova
```{r}
kable(summary(strengthmodel)$fstatistic)
```

##Testing for significance of contrasts
Contrast 1 is PT - different versus control and PT - same; Contrast 2 is control versus PT - same
```{r, fig.margin=TRUE}
kable(tidy(strengthmodel))
```


#Calculate F's from t's (t-statistics above)
We also calculate the F statistics, in order to report the statistics in consistent way for those more familiar with SPSS outputs.

Contrast 1:
```{r}
contrast1F = 6.79^2
contrast1F
```
Contrast 2:
```{r}
contrast2F = 2.03^2
contrast2F
```


As predicted, original condition affected quality ratings in the follow-up session, F(2, 852) = 24.87, p < .001. Participants in the control and perspective-taking/same ideology conditions viewed their arguments as higher quality than did participants in the perspective-taking/different ideology condition, F(1, 852) = 46.10, p < .001. Participants also saw their arguments as higher quality in the perspective-taking/same ideology rather than control condition, F(1, 852) = 4.12, p = .04

```{r strength_graph}
se_plus <- function(x) mean(x) + sqrt(var(x)/length(x))
se_minus <- function(x) mean(x) - sqrt(var(x)/length(x))

limits <- aes(ymax = se_u, ymin= se_l)
dodge <- position_dodge(width=0.9)

summary <- d %>%
  dplyr::group_by(condition) %>%
  dplyr::summarise("Argument_Strength_Self" = mean(strengthIndex, na.rm=TRUE), "se_u"=se_plus(strengthIndex), "se_l"=se_minus(strengthIndex))

plot <- ggplot(data=summary, aes(x=condition, y=Argument_Strength_Self, fill=condition)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  geom_errorbar(limits, position=dodge, width=0.25) +
  guides(fill=FALSE) +
  labs(x="Condition", y="Argument Strength (Self)") +
  theme_hc() + 
  theme(text=element_text(family="Calibri", size=14)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#ffad99", "#05C68A", "#17699E")) + 
  scale_x_discrete(labels=c("Control", "Perspective Taking\nDifferent", "Perspective Taking\nSame"))
  
#GRAPH1
#plot
#ggsave("Study_2_StrengthSelf.png", scale=1, width=133, height=100, units="mm", dpi=1000)
```
\newpage

# T2 - Value Congruence Judgements

Value congruence is measured as in the main study.

```{r}
congruenceItems <- dplyr::select(d, Q7.congruent, Q8.worldview, Q9.morals)
alphaCongruence <- psych::alpha(congruenceItems)
kable(alphaCongruence$total)
```

Because of our high alpha (alpha = 0.96), we consider the value congruence items as an index
```{r}
d$congruenceIndex <- 8 - (d$Q7.congruent + d$Q8.worldview + d$Q9.morals)/3
```

#Effect of condition on T2 perceived value congruence

```{r}
contrasts(d$condition) <- cbind(c(-1, 2, -1), c(+1, 0, -1))
congru_model <- lm(congruenceIndex ~ condition, d)
```

##Omnibus Anova
```{r}
kable(summary(congru_model)$fstatistic)
```

##Testing for significance of contrasts
Contrast 1 is PT - different versus control and PT - same; Contrast 2 is control versus PT - same
```{r, fig.margin=TRUE}
kable(tidy(congru_model))
```

#Calculate F's from t's (t-statistics above)
We also calculate the F statistics, in order to report the statistics in consistent way for those more familiar with SPSS outputs.

Contrast 1:
```{r}
contrast1F = 7.31^2
contrast1F
```
Contrast 2:
```{r}
contrast2F = 1.25^2
contrast2F
```


As predicted, original condition affected value congruence ratings in the follow-up session, F(2, 852) = 27.29, p < .001. Participants in the control and perspective-taking/same ideology conditions viewed their arguments as more value congruent than did participants in the perspective-taking/different ideology condition, F(1, 852) = 53.43, p < .001. Participants did not see their arguments as significantly different from the perspective-taking/same ideology in the control condition, F(1, 852) = 1.56, p = .21

```{r value_graph}
se_plus <- function(x) mean(x) + sqrt(var(x)/length(x))
se_minus <- function(x) mean(x) - sqrt(var(x)/length(x))

limits <- aes(ymax = se_u, ymin= se_l)
dodge <- position_dodge(width=0.9)

summary <- d %>%
  dplyr::group_by(condition) %>%
  dplyr::summarise("Value_Congruence" = mean(congruenceIndex, na.rm=TRUE), "se_u"=se_plus(congruenceIndex), "se_l"=se_minus(congruenceIndex))

plot <- ggplot(data=summary, aes(x=condition, y=Value_Congruence, fill=condition)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  geom_errorbar(limits, position=dodge, width=0.25) +
  guides(fill=FALSE) +
  labs(x="Condition", y="Value Congruence") +
  theme_hc() + 
  theme(text=element_text(family="Calibri", size=14)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#ffad99", "#05C68A", "#17699E")) + 
  scale_x_discrete(labels=c("Control", "Perspective Taking\nDifferent", "Perspective Taking\nSame"))
  
#GRAPH2
#plot
#ggsave("Study_2_ValueCongruence.png", scale=1, width=133, height=100, units="mm", dpi=1000)
```

\newpage

#Mediation Analysis

Does value congruence mediate the effect of condition on perceived argument strength? We use the same mediation analysis strategy as in the main study. 

```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, comment=NA}
library(mediation)

d$strength_s <- scale(d$strengthIndex, center=FALSE, scale=TRUE)
d$congruence_s <- as.numeric(scale(d$congruenceIndex))
```

```{r}
d$H1 <- 1
d$H1 <- ifelse(d$condition == "PT-same", 1, d$H1)
d$H1 <- ifelse(d$condition == "control", 1, d$H1)
d$H1 <- ifelse(d$condition == "PT-different", -2, d$H1)

d$H2 <- 0
d$H2 <- ifelse(d$condition == "PT-same", 1, d$H2)
d$H2 <- ifelse(d$condition == "control", -1, d$H2)
```


# Mediation Model: Condition -> Value Congruence -> Strength

## Contrast 1: Control and PT-Same verus PT-Different
```{r, cache=TRUE}
modelm <- lm(congruence_s ~ H1 + H2, data=d)

modely <- lm(strengthIndex ~ H1 + congruence_s + H2, data=d)

med_model <- mediation::mediate(modelm, modely, treat="H1",
                                sims=5000,
                                boot=TRUE,
                   mediator="congruence_s")

summary(med_model)
```

The effect of condition on the difference between control and PT-same versus PT-different was mediated by value-congruence (ab = 0.09, 95% CI = .06 to .11). 

## Contrast 2: Control versus PT-Same

```{r, cache=TRUE}
med_model <- mediation::mediate(modelm, modely, treat="H2",
                                sims=5000,
                                boot=TRUE,
                   mediator="congruence_s")

summary(med_model)
```

However the difference between PT-same and control effect was not mediated by value-congruence (ab = .02, 95% CI = -.01 to .07).

#Save Data Set
```{r}
write.csv(d, "Study 2 Posttest Other Evaluation Merged Data.csv")
```

#Post-test Part 2: Objective 3rd party argument analysis

#Read in T2 - Objective Ratings

```{r}
#Read in evaluations
d_objeval <- read.csv("T2 objective evaluations clean.csv")

#Evaluations for any argument that was evaluated in original set
d_evaluations <- merge(d_T1, d_objeval, by = "MID", all=FALSE)
d_evaluations2 <- d_evaluations %>%
  filter(Exclude..y != "Y")

#Anything that was evaluated twice, remove the second
d_evaluations3 <- d_evaluations2[!duplicated(d_evaluations2$MID),] %>%
  filter(!is.na(condition)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(evaluator_MID))
```

```{r}
d <- d_evaluations3

d$condition <- as.factor(d$condition)
contrasts(d$condition) <- cbind(c(-1, 2, -1), c(+1, 0, -1))
```


# Argument Strength Index

Argument strength is measured using the same 6 items as for the self-evaluations. As always, we begin by computing alpha.

```{r}
strengthItems <- dplyr::select(d, persuasive, convincing, reasonable, strong, thoughtful, wellformulated)
alphaStrength <- psych::alpha(strengthItems)
kable(alphaStrength$total)
```

Because they load together (alpha = 0.95), we consider them as an index.

```{r}
d$strengthIndex <- (d$persuasive + d$convincing + d$reasonable + d$strong + d$thoughtful + d$wellformulated)/6
```

# Effect of condition on objective strength

```{r}
d <- d %>%
  filter(is.na(d$strengthIndex) == FALSE)
```

```{r}
strength_model <- lm(strengthIndex ~ condition, d)
```

##Omnibus Anova
```{r}
kable(summary(strength_model)$fstatistic)
```

##Testing for significance of contrasts
Contrast 1 is PT - different versus control and PT - same; Contrast 2 is control versus PT - same
```{r, fig.margin=TRUE}
kable(tidy(strength_model))
```

#Calculate F's from t's (t-statistics above)
We also calculate the F statistics, in order to report the statistics in consistent way for those more familiar with SPSS outputs.

Contrast 1:
```{r}
contrast1F = 1.10^2
contrast1F
```
Contrast 2:
```{r}
contrast2F = 0.79^2
contrast2F
```


Original condition did not affect value congruence ratings in the follow-up session, F(2, 1205) = 0.93, p = .39. Participants in the control and perspective-taking/same ideology conditions did not differ in strength evaluations from participants in the perspective-taking/different ideology condition, F(1, 1205) = 1.21, p =.27. Participants also did not see their arguments as significantly different from the perspective-taking/same ideology in the control condition, F(1, 1205) = .62, p = .43.


```{r strength_other_graph}
se_plus <- function(x) mean(x) + sqrt(var(x)/length(x))
se_minus <- function(x) mean(x) - sqrt(var(x)/length(x))

limits <- aes(ymax = se_u, ymin= se_l)
dodge <- position_dodge(width=0.9)

summary <- d %>%
  dplyr::group_by(condition) %>%
  dplyr::summarise("Argument_Strength_Other" = mean(strengthIndex, na.rm=TRUE), "se_u"=se_plus(strengthIndex), "se_l"=se_minus(strengthIndex))

plot <- ggplot(data=summary, aes(x=condition, y=Argument_Strength_Other, fill=condition)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  geom_errorbar(limits, position=dodge, width=0.25) +

  labs(x="Condition", y="Argument Strength (Other)") +

  theme(text=element_text(family="Calibri", size=14)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#ffad99", "#05C68A", "#17699E")) + 
  scale_x_discrete(labels=c("Control", "Perspective Taking\nDifferent", "Perspective Taking\nSame"))
```
